title: DARPA Total Information Awareness → Palantir (claimed)
summary: Total Information Awareness (later Terrorism Information Awareness) was a DARPA data-mining research program run by the Information Awareness Office, set up in January 2002 under John Poindexter. Congress barred funding for it in the FY2004 defense appropriations act, signed Sept 30, 2003, while a classified annex kept some counterterrorism analysis tools for foreign intelligence. National Journal reported in 2006 that key TIA projects moved, renamed, to an NSA-linked research office: a government-to-government continuation. Palantir, incorporated in 2003 and backed by Peter Thiel and reportedly In-Q-Tel, is often called TIA's private successor, but no transfer of TIA code, staff or contracts to Palantir is documented.

claims.claim: TIA did not really end in 2003; its research continued inside the government under new names.
claims.explanation: The statute itself (Sec. 8131 of the FY2004 defense appropriations act) barred TIA funding but exempted 'processing, analysis, and collaboration tools for counterterrorism foreign intelligence' described in a classified annex, and Government Executive reported less controversial technologies were moved elsewhere in DARPA. In February 2006 National Journal (Shane Harris) reported that TIA's core prototype was renamed 'Basketball' and Genoa II renamed 'Topsail', moved to a research office serving NSA, often under the same contracts with SAIC and Hicks & Associates. That continuation is reported, not officially confirmed, and it was public-to-public: it moved to other agencies, not to a private successor.

claims.claim: Palantir is TIA's private successor: the program was taken out of DARPA and continued as Palantir.
claims.explanation: Washingtonian (Shane Harris, 2012) reports that soon after Palantir's 2004 launch, Richard Perle arranged for Alex Karp and Peter Thiel to meet John Poindexter, TIA's former head; Karp says Poindexter was one of many experts the founders consulted, and Harris notes Palantir's approach bore 'striking similarities' to TIA's. In-Q-Tel, the CIA's venture arm, reportedly invested about $2 million. None of this shows that TIA's code, staff, contracts or funding went to Palantir: Poindexter is not reported to have taken any role at the company, and In-Q-Tel is a CIA vehicle, not DARPA. The documented continuation of TIA work went to NSA-linked offices and contractors such as SAIC, not to Palantir.
